sections.html:
Cedar City is the largest city in Iron County, in southwestern Utah, about 250 miles south of Salt Lake City and 170 miles north of Las Vegas along Interstate 15. It sits above 5,600 feet in Cedar Valley, with St. George about 50 miles southwest. Zion, Bryce Canyon and Cedar Breaks are all a day trip away.

The population was 35,235 in 2020 and is estimated at 41,871 for July 2025, with 11,824 households and 12,723 housing units at the last full count. The median age is 26.2, a reflection of Southern Utah University. A young population means plenty of rentals, which matters if you are a landlord thinking of selling. Demand for houses and rentals also tends to follow the school calendar and the festival season, so think about timing before you set a closing date.

The climate is semi-arid, with about 11 inches of precipitation a year and about 47.8 inches of snow. January highs average 42.8 degrees and lows 18.0, July highs average 91.0, and the record low is minus 26. That range is hard on exteriors: freeze and thaw cracks driveways and stucco, dry summers fade roofing, and cold nights stress older plumbing and water heaters. A buyer touring in winter will notice insulation, windows and heating cost fast.

  • Roof condition after heavy snow seasons
  • Exposed pipes and hose bibs in cold snaps
  • Cracks in concrete and stucco
  • Heating system age and efficiency

A vacant house needs attention in both seasons. An empty one can freeze its pipes in winter and collect dust and weeds in summer.

City Hall is at 10 North Main Street, open 8 am to 5 pm. The City Council meets Wednesdays at 5:30 pm and streams on YouTube, except on the fifth Wednesday of a month. The city offers a water usage app called MY360 that lets residents view their water use, which helps when you close out an account.

Interstate 15 is the main route, a Union Pacific branch line runs along the western edge of town, and Cedar City Regional Airport has Delta Connection flights. A local bus system also operates.

sections.h2: How Iron County assesses and bills property tax
sections.html:
Iron County values and bills Cedar City homes from its offices at 68 South 100 East in Parowan. Property is valued by condition and ownership as of January 1, using cost, income and market approaches. The Assessor's number is 435-477-8310.

Iron County property tax calendar
StepTiming
Notice of Valuation and Taxes mailedAround July 22
Board of Equalization appeals dueSeptember 15, 5:00 PM (or 45 days after the notice, if later)
Property tax notices mailedAround November 1
Tax payment due statewideNovember 30

A primary residence is taxed on 55 percent of value, and Utah Code 59-2-103 limits the reduction to one acre of land per residential unit. Current-year taxes that go unpaid become delinquent on December 1, and parcels left unpaid for years can end up at a tax sale. If you owe back taxes, talk to the treasurer before you list.

Appeals go through the Iron County Auditor at 435-477-8333. The Board of Equalization is usually in session from late September through early October. The assessed value is presumed correct, so you need firm evidence of a lower market value, such as recent comparable sales, an appraisal or a documented error in the county record.

Keep paying the bill by November 30 while an appeal is open. If the house sells during the process, tell the buyer's side what is pending so the title company can route any refund.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale skip?
sections.html:
Selling for cash leaves out the lender appraisal and the list of buyer repair requests. Here is how it runs.

  1. You describe the house and any tenants, liens or repairs.
  2. You get an offer and decide whether to take it.
  3. A title company searches title and arranges payoffs.
  4. You sign at a date you choose and are paid at closing.

Before you call, find your latest Iron County tax notice, lease dates for any tenant, and mortgage payoff details. If the house has been empty through winter, mention it, since the buyer will inspect for freeze damage.

sections.h2: What Cedar City sellers usually face
sections.html:
Many sellers here own a rental that has aged, a house that needs updating, or a property inherited from a relative who lived out of state. Selling for cash fits those cases because nobody is waiting on a lender and there is no list of requested repairs.

  • Student and seasonal rentals with turnover damage
  • Houses with older roofs, windows and heating systems
  • Inherited property where heirs live in other states
  • Vacant houses that sit empty through a cold winter

Most of these sellers want one clear closing date instead of months of showings. Share lease dates and rent details early so move-out terms are agreed in writing.

faqs.q: What county is Cedar City in, and who sets my property value?
faqs.a: Iron County, through the Iron County Assessor. The office is at 68 South 100 East in Parowan, phone 435-477-8310.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Cedar City property value?
faqs.a: Iron County appeals are due September 15 by 5:00 PM, or 45 days after the valuation notice is mailed if that is later. File through the Iron County Auditor at 435-477-8333.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Cedar City?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, and notices are mailed around November 1.
It had 35,235 residents in 2020 and an estimated 41,871 in July 2025, making it the largest city in Iron County.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in Cedar City with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes, with tenants in place or after they leave. Share lease dates and rent details early so the closing date and move-out terms are set in writing.
